program.name: ENS Service Provider Program, Season 3 (SPP3)
program.authority: ENS DAO, following a named SPP3 committee recommendation ratified by on-chain executable vote

rules.description: The public cohort record states that one application failed the eligibility gate and the remaining 25 were scored; Namespace appears among the scored and selected providers. This record therefore represents only the aggregate fact that Namespace passed the published pre-score hard screen, without asserting gate-by-gate results or a check timestamp.

eligibility.rationale: Eligibility status is derived from the public process statement that only applications passing the hard screen were scored and from Namespace appearing in the published scored cohort. The exact eligibility-check time was not identified in reviewed public sources.

evaluators.role: Chair; substitute scorer for Namespace following a member recusal

evaluators.recusalReason: The public cohort record discloses a conflict-of-interest recusal for Namespace; the underlying conflict facts are not stated in the reviewed public sources.

evaluators.role: ENS Labs Technical Representative and voting Committee Member

conflicts.description: The public cohort record states that sovereignsignal.eth was recused from Namespace evaluation under the program conflict-of-interest rules.
conflicts.resolution: The Chair's independently prepared scores replaced the recused scoring input for Namespace, preserving four scoring inputs.

conflicts.description: The public cohort record states that sovereignsignal.eth was recused from the Namespace committee vote.
conflicts.resolution: The member did not participate in the Namespace committee vote. The reviewed public sources do not establish that a substitute voter was used.

evidence.description: SPP3 program authorization and committee model, including objectives, authority separation, quorum, voting, conflict rules, evaluation floor, and provider obligations.
Published SPP3 submission timeline, hard eligibility screen, and weighted evaluation rubric.
Published SPP3 cohort recommendation, Namespace award and rationale, aggregate scores, recusal disclosure, process notes, and delivery prerequisites.
Public proposal mirror reporting the SPP3 cohort recommendation as executed, including vote totals, quorum display, and vote end time.

Namespace application URI linked by the public cohort recommendation. The content was not successfully retrieved during this reconstruction, and no application-content claim in this record depends on it.

criteria.name: Discretion: Team and Budget Fit
criteria.scoreScale: 1-5; public cohort assessment excludes this component from the published weighted subtotal

materialFindings.statement: The published committee assessment reports Namespace C1 Prior Delivery mean score as 4.1.
The published committee assessment reports Namespace C2 Scope Clarity mean score as 3.4.
The published committee assessment reports Namespace C3 Milestone Structure mean score as 3.3.
The published committee assessment reports Namespace C4 Adoption, Revenue, and Ecosystem Utility mean score as 3.5.
The published committee assessment reports Namespace weighted subtotal as 3.43, with the 5% discretionary component excluded and the subtotal therefore out of 4.75.

The committee recommended a $500,000 Namespace award based on its subname infrastructure role, prior delivery, ENSv2 migration work, continued tooling maintenance, and business-development scope, while noting milestone dependency on ENSv2 mainnet timing.

evaluation.aggregateScale: published weighted subtotal out of 4.75; 5% discretionary component excluded

decision.rationale: The executed cohort proposal ratified the four selected SPP3 providers. Namespace was allocated $500,000 following the committee recommendation and published assessment.
decision.quorum: 130.99% displayed by the public proposal mirror

challenge.scope: The reviewed public governing and cohort artifacts did not identify a dedicated post-decision factual or procedural correction path for this provider-selection decision. This is a public-evidence statement, not a claim that no private or internal process existed.

deliveryConditions.description: Operate under the negotiated SPP3 Award Notice and maintain the required reporting cadence during the funded cycle; continued engagement and reporting are the public program conditions for stream continuation.
deliveryConditions.reviewWindow: Quarterly reporting across the 12-month SPP3 cycle
deliveryConditions.verificationMethod: Published or institutionally reviewed quarterly reporting and committee/Foundation oversight under the SPP3 terms and Award Notice.
deliveryConditions.verifier: SPP3 committee and ENS Foundation, according to the public program terms and provider Award Notice
dependencies: Successful KYC checkpoint and signed Award Notice before stream activation
deliveryConditions.consequence: The public program terms permit stream suspension or termination for abandonment, reporting failure, or other defined breaches, subject to notice/response terms in the agreement.

notes: Public-only retrospective reconstruction; this is not a contemporaneous institutional decision record.

governingPolicy.effectiveAt and eligibility.checkedAt are intentionally null because exact timestamps were not established from the reviewed public sources. The resulting schema findings are preserved rather than repaired with invented dates.
The public cohort report states that individual scoring records remain internal working documents. Aggregate committee scores are represented; no undisclosed individual score is inferred.

The public cohort report discloses sovereignsignal.eth's recusal from Namespace evaluation and vote. It states that the Chair's scores replace the recused scoring input; it does not state that a substitute voter replaced the recused member in the committee vote, so those surfaces are represented separately.
The linked Namespace application URI was not successfully retrieved during reconstruction. No applicant-content claim in this record is inferred from inaccessible content.
The public timeline artifacts are not silently reconciled: the May 14 timeline lists submissions closing June 9, while the later cohort process narrative says submissions closed June 4.
